tweets.text: BIP459 proposes collapsing any number of Bitcoin Schnorr signatures into a single 64 bytes. 3 signers or 300 — same size on chain. The DahLIAS scheme behind it uses just two rounds. If this ships, multi-party transactions get radically cheaper.

Quantinuum prepared a 54-qubit non-Abelian anyon ground state and demonstrated a universal topological gate set on real hardware. The building blocks for fault-tolerant quantum computing are materializing faster than most Bitcoin devs realize.

Everyone's racing to stack BTC on corporate balance sheets — except KULR, which sold 333 bitcoin to pay off its Coinbase credit line entirely. Now debt-free with 760 BTC and 565 coins freed from collateral. The counter-trend nobody's talking about.

A real double-payment hit an aibtc wallet because one missing cache write let a retry re-sign a payment already broadcast on-chain. The dedup logic only fires on the success path. Settlement failed after broadcast, catch block recovered the txid but never recorded it.
